RmlUi, vendored for VaCuusRml
=============================

upstream: https://github.com/mikke89/RmlUi
commit:   0ae381e00d7426762bb5ed897973366358b16642
vendored: 2026-07-29

VENDORED_SHA.txt NEXT TO THIS FILE HOLDS THAT SHA AND NOTHING ELSE, and must keep
holding nothing else: Tools/gen_rcss_matrix.py:43,180 reads the whole file and
.strip()s it into the generated docs/buyer/rcss-matrix.md header. This file is the
human half -- what is here, and the local patches. Read both before re-vendoring.

What is here, and why exactly this
----------------------------------
Vendored per docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-vacuus-m1-render-spike.md:114-122:

    cp -r Include Source Backends LICENSE.txt readme.md $DEST/
    rm -rf $DEST/Source/Lua $DEST/Source/SVG $DEST/Source/Lottie
    echo "<sha>" > $DEST/VENDORED_SHA.txt

Backends/ is reference material and is never compiled. Only Source/Core is built,
through the per-file relay .cpp files that Source/VaCuusRml/Private/Gen/ generates:
gen_relays.sh walks Source/Core alone, so all 190 relays there are relay_Core_*.cpp,
one per .cpp under Source/Core. Source/Debugger is vendored and SHIPS as source -- its
LICENSE.txt is a disclosure Tools/fab_inventory.sh asserts reaches the package -- but no
module compiles it and nothing in the plugin names RmlUi/Debugger.h or Rml::Debugger.

Local patches
-------------
This tree was byte-identical to the upstream commit above until 2026-08-03.
Re-vendoring procedure: copy the file list above from the pinned commit, reapply
the patch(es) below, then run the verification named with each one -- a patch
that is silently lost re-introduces a defect nobody can see on screen. A patch
whose entry names the upstream commit it backports (#7 is the first) is DROPPED,
not reapplied, once the pinned SHA is at or after that commit; its verification
must still pass, and a doubled hunk is exactly what it cannot see.

Patch #1 -- data-style compares against the unit-less variant (bead VaCuus-akj.17).

Source/Core/DataViewDefault.cpp, DataViewStyle::Update. Upstream decides whether a
data-style binding needs re-applying by comparing the incoming string against
`p->Get<String>()`, and Property::Get<T> forwards straight to the property's value
Variant (Include/RmlUi/Core/Property.h:41-45), which does not carry the unit -- that
is a separate member (Property.h:50-51). So the property parsed out of "100px" reads
back as "100" and never compares equal to the string that produced it. Every dirty of
the bound variable therefore called Element::SetProperty with an unchanged value, and
SetProperty does not compare either (ElementStyle.cpp:642-654 -> PropertyDictionary
::SetProperty + DirtyProperty, unconditional), nor does ComputeValues, which returns
the DIRTY set rather than a changed-value set (ElementStyle.cpp:1060-1064). So the
element restyles, and a layout property relayouts the whole document, every time.

Whether that also costs a PUBLISHED frame depends on which property is bound, and the
first version of the test below got this wrong -- it bound `width`, and passed with
the patch reverted. Two RmlUi shortcuts absorb the layout-only path: an unchanged box
never reaches OnResize, and ElementText reuses its compiled geometry when the
regenerated mesh compares equal (ElementText.cpp:541-547). The border/background path
has no such check -- ElementBackgroundBorder::GenerateGeometry releases and re-makes
its mesh unconditionally (ElementBackgroundBorder.cpp:181-187) -- so a no-op write to
border-*-width, border-radius or box-shadow is a fresh handle plus resource traffic,
both legs of VaCuus's publish gate. A HUD whose model dirties a coarse top-level name
each tick (FVaCuusBoundModel::ApplyUpdate dirties the ROOT of a nested field) then
published EVERY frame while nothing on it changed: measured 100 of 100.

Not fixed at the VaCuus layer, because it cannot be: the plugin never sees this
call. Factory::RegisterDataViewInstancer refuses a duplicate name and logs a warning
(Source/Core/Factory.cpp:561-567), so "style" cannot be shadowed by our own view;
Element::SetProperty is not virtual (Include/RmlUi/Core/Element.h:177), so no custom
element instancer can intercept it; and DataModel::DirtyVariable takes top-level
names only, so the coarse dirty that exposes this cannot be narrowed either.

Verification: automation test VaCuus.Model.View.DataStyleIdle
(Source/VaCuusRender/Private/Tests/VaCuusDataStyleIdleTest.cpp) drives a real view
whose model dirties a sibling field every frame while the bound style values stay
"4px" (border-left-width) and "120px" (width), and asserts ZERO published frames over
100. Revert this hunk and it fails with exactly the numbers a re-vendor that dropped
the patch would produce:

  Expected 'and the unit-bearing data-style bindings published NOT ONE of them
  (akj.17)' to be 0, but it was 100.
  Expected 'the new values settle back to zero published frames' to be 0, but it
  was 20.

The hunk, ABRIDGED -- the in-file comment is long enough that reproducing it here
twice would be the thing that rots. One line changes:

--- a/Source/Core/DataViewDefault.cpp
+++ b/Source/Core/DataViewDefault.cpp
@@ bool DataViewStyle::Update(DataModel& model)
 	if (element && GetExpression().Run(expr_interface, variant))
 	{
 		const String value = variant.Get<String>();
 		const Property* p = element->GetLocalProperty(property_name);
-		if (!p || p->Get<String>() != value)
+		/* VaCuus patch #1 comment -- see the file for the full text */
+		if (!p || p->ToString() != value)
 		{
 			element->SetProperty(property_name, value);
 			result = true;
 		}
 	}

Property::ToString() re-appends the unit and maps a keyword back to its name
(Source/Core/Property.cpp:12-20 -> PropertyDefinition::GetValue,
Source/Core/PropertyDefinition.cpp:91-135), so the comparison is now against the
string that produced the property. It is a strict widening of the equal case: it can
only make MORE comparisons succeed, never fewer, because a property's ToString is
the string a re-parse would produce. Values whose ToString is not the authored
spelling still compare unequal exactly as they did before, and re-set exactly as
often: colours other than lowercase #rrggbb (TypeConverter.cpp:267-273 spells a
Colourb that way), shorthands (no local property exists under the shorthand's own
name), and spellings that "%.3f" with trimmed trailing zeros cannot reproduce
("120.50px"). Those residues are documented for buyers in docs/buyer/perf-guide.md.

NOT yet offered upstream -- that is a maintainer action and nobody has taken it.
It should be: the hunk is upstream-shaped on purpose, and until it lands there
every re-vendor has to carry it by hand.


Patch #2 -- dll-interface removed from four HEADER-ONLY CLASS TEMPLATES (Win64 pass,
2026-08-03). Found by the plugin's first Windows build ever; invisible on Linux and
macOS by construction.

    Include/RmlUi/Core/ObserverPtr.h:42            class RMLUICORE_API ObserverPtr
    Include/RmlUi/Core/ObserverPtr.h:113           class RMLUICORE_API EnableObserverPtr
    Include/RmlUi/Core/UniqueRenderResource.h:14   class RMLUICORE_API UniqueRenderResource
    Include/RmlUi/Core/Traits.h:35                 class RMLUICORE_API Releaser

In each, `class RMLUICORE_API X` becomes `class X`. Nothing else changes.

THE MECHANISM. Include/RmlUi/Core/Header.h:8-21: in a shared build on Win32,
RMLUICORE_API is __declspec(dllexport) while compiling the library (RMLUI_CORE_EXPORTS
is set for VaCuusRml) and __declspec(dllimport) for everyone else. On a CLASS TEMPLATE
that is a category error. dllimport tells MSVC the members of every instantiation live
in another DLL, so a consumer TU stops instantiating them locally and emits __imp_
references instead -- which resolve only if the library happened to instantiate and
export that exact specialization. VaCuusJs asks for one the library never used:

    VaCuusJsDom.cpp.obj : error LNK2019: unresolved external symbol
    "__declspec(dllimport) public: __cdecl Rml::ObserverPtr<class Rml::Element>::
    ObserverPtr<class Rml::Element>(void)" (__imp_??0?$ObserverPtr@VElement@Rml@@@Rml@@QEAA@XZ)
    referenced in function "public: struct JSValue __cdecl
    FVaCuusJsViewContext::WrapElement(class Rml::Element *)"

Rml::Element is used constantly, but nothing inside RmlUi's own Core ever
default-constructs an ObserverPtr<Element>, so that one constructor was never emitted
into UnrealEditor-VaCuusRml.dll and never exported.

WHY REMOVING IT IS CORRECT RATHER THAN A WORKAROUND. All four templates are entirely
header-inline: no .cpp in Source/ defines a member of any of them, and the library
contains no explicit instantiation of any of them (both checked). A header-only
template needs no dll-interface at all -- every module compiles its own copy, which is
the normal C++ model. The non-template API those copies call IS still exported and
still carries the macro: ObserverPtrBlock plus AllocateObserverPtrBlock and
DeallocateObserverPtrBlockIfEmpty (ObserverPtr.h:10-15). The observer STATE therefore
stays single-instance in VaCuusRml.dll, which is the property that actually matters;
only the inline code around it is duplicated per module.

Off Windows the macro expands to __attribute__((visibility("default")))
(Header.h:45), which on a header-only template only widens symbol visibility for code
each module already instantiates for itself. That is why Linux and macOS linked
happily for six milestones with the defect present, and it is also why removing it
cannot change their behaviour: no cross-module reference to these inline members
exists on any platform.

VERIFICATION (the re-vendoring check for this patch): build any Win64 MODULAR target
-- e.g. `Build.bat <Project>Editor Win64 Development -project=...`. With the patch
reverted, UnrealEditor-VaCuusJs.dll fails to link with the LNK2019 above. With it
applied, all five plugin DLLs link. Seen both ways on 2026-08-03. A monolithic Win64
target does NOT exercise this: VaCuusRml.Build.cs defines RMLUI_STATIC_LIB there, and
Header.h:51 then makes RMLUICORE_API empty, so the defect cannot appear.

NOT yet offered upstream -- same standing as patch #1. It should be; the fix is
upstream-shaped and costs upstream nothing.


Patch #3 -- box-shadow renders an opaque white rectangle and republishes every frame
when SaveLayerAsTexture is not implemented (beads VaCuus-u0q, VaCuus-iuv).

Four files, four hunks. This is one fix; carrying any hunk without the others is worse
than carrying none, and the middle paragraph below says exactly why.

  Include/RmlUi/Core/CallbackTexture.h   CallbackTextureInterface::SaveLayerAsTexture
  Source/Core/CallbackTexture.cpp        same, definition
  Source/Core/GeometryBoxShadow.cpp      the texture callback's return
  Source/Core/ElementBackgroundBorder.cpp  GenerateGeometry, and the Texture.h include
                                           at :10 that hunk 3 needs to compile

THE DEFECT IS UPSTREAM'S, not ours, and it fires for ANY backend that leaves
SaveLayerAsTexture at its optional default -- which the base class explicitly permits by
returning a zero handle (Source/Core/RenderInterface.cpp:37-40). Two things then go wrong
at once, and the second one hides behind the first:

  (a) THE WHITE RECTANGLE. ElementBackgroundBorder::GenerateGeometry commits to the
      box-shadow path on `computed.has_box_shadow()` alone: it ERASES the element's normal
      background and border and stores a BoxShadowRenderable instead. Render() then draws
      that renderable's `geometry` -- a premultiplied WHITE quad covering the border box
      extended by 1.5*blur+spread (Source/Core/BoxShadowCache.cpp:56-59) -- textured with
      the null handle. VaCuus's replayer binds GWhiteTexture and clears bUseTexture for
      handle 0 (VaCuusReplayRenderer.cpp:1139-1145), so the quad comes out as pure vertex
      colour: an opaque white box where the element's own background and border should be.

  (b) THE FRAME-RATE CHURN. The texture callback returns true whether or not it produced
      a handle (Source/Core/GeometryBoxShadow.cpp, the old `return true` after
      SaveLayerAsTexture), so CallbackTextureDatabase::EnsureLoaded sees neither a handle
      nor load_failed and re-runs the WHOLE callback on every frame that asks for the
      texture (Source/Core/TextureDatabase.cpp:46-60): a layer pushed, a blur filter
      compiled and released, geometry made and released. That is permanent resource
      traffic, which permanently trips FVaCuusCommandBuffer::HasResourceTraffic() and
      forces a published frame every tick on a document that never changes.

THE HUNKS.

1. CallbackTextureInterface::SaveLayerAsTexture returns bool instead of void -- true only
   when a texture handle was really produced. Purely additive (an ignored return still
   compiles), and upstream-shaped: its sibling GenerateTexture already returns bool with
   the same meaning, and CallbackTextureFunction's own doc comment promises "@return True
   on success" (CallbackTexture.h:19), which the box-shadow callback could not honour
   without this.

2. GeometryBoxShadow's callback returns that bool instead of an unconditional true. Fixes
   (b): one failure latches load_failed and the callback never runs again for that cache
   entry.

3. ElementBackgroundBorder::GenerateGeometry PROBES the shadow texture (Texture::
   GetDimensions, which is what forces the callback) and falls through to the ordinary
   background/border path when no texture was produced. Fixes (a).

   It deliberately does NOT render BoxShadowRenderable::background_border_geometry, which
   looks like the obvious substitute: BoxShadowCache::GetHandle premultiplies that mesh's
   colours WITHOUT opacity (BoxShadowCache.cpp:85-91, opacity instead going into the shadow
   quad's vertex alpha at :57-58), so at opacity < 1 it would render fully opaque. The
   normal path premultiplies by opacity and is exactly right.

4. THE REFUSED RENDERABLE IS PARKED on the ordinary background instead of being dropped.
   THIS IS THE HUNK THAT LOOKS LIKE BOOKKEEPING AND IS NOT -- the first version of this
   patch omitted it and was caught by its own test. BoxShadowCache holds entries by WeakPtr
   and erases the entry from the renderable's destructor (BoxShadowCache.cpp:13, :65-77),
   so letting the SharedPtr die at the end of GenerateGeometry destroys the cache entry and
   with it the CallbackTexture whose load_failed hunk 2 just set. Every subsequent restyle
   then minted a fresh entry and re-ran the whole callback -- (b) again, gated on restyle
   instead of on frame. Measured: 70 refusals across 70 restyled frames, versus 1.

WHY THIS IS NOT FIXED AT THE VaCuus LAYER, checked rather than assumed. The obvious move
is to refuse the PROPERTY, so `has_box_shadow()` is never true. It cannot be done:
StyleSheetSpecification::RegisterParser REFUSES to overwrite an existing name -- it logs
"Parser with name %s already exists!" and returns false (StyleSheetSpecification.cpp:99-110)
-- so the registered "box_shadow" parser (:245) cannot be shadowed by one of ours. There is
no capability query on RenderInterface to add either without breaking the reference
backends, which override SaveLayerAsTexture but would not override a new predicate.

WHAT THE PLUGIN CONTRIBUTES, and it must land with these hunks: the recorder now OVERRIDES
both layer-capture virtuals rather than inheriting them, returning 0 with one latched
Warning per view that names the property, the reason and the substitute
(VaCuusRecordingRenderInterface.cpp, SaveLayerAsTexture/SaveLayerAsMaskImage). Without
hunks 3 and 4 that return value is destructive; without the override the failure is silent.

VERIFICATION (the re-vendoring check): automation tests
VaCuus.Render.LayerCapture.Refused and VaCuus.Render.LayerCapture.RestyleChurn
(Source/VaCuusRender/Private/Tests/VaCuusLayerCaptureTest.cpp). Each hunk has been reverted
alone and watched to fail:

  - hunks 2+3 reverted (the true pre-fix state): Refused never settles --
    "still publishing after 200 frames (201 published, 201 recorded)".
  - hunk 3 reverted alone: "Expected 'and draws no opaque-white quad ...' to be 0, but it
    was 12" (three shadowed elements, four corners each).
  - hunk 2 reverted alone: RestyleChurn reports "to be 10, but it was 70" -- one refusal
    per restyled frame. NOTE that Refused still PASSES in this state, which is not what one
    would guess: once hunk 3 declines the shadow path, an idle document never asks for the
    texture again. That is exactly why RestyleChurn exists.
  - hunk 4 omitted: same 10 -> 70 as above.

MASK-IMAGE IS NOT FIXED HERE, only made loud (bead VaCuus-iuv). SaveLayerAsMaskImage needs
the same layer capture, and there is nothing to make harmless short of implementing it: the
mask decorators are drawn BEFORE the capture (Source/Core/ElementEffects.cpp:300-305), so
with layers skipped at replay the mask artwork lands in the frame and paints over the
element. Verified on screen, not inferred.

NOT yet offered upstream -- same standing as patches #1 and #2. Hunks 1-3 are
upstream-shaped and fix a real upstream defect for any optional-feature-skipping backend;
hunk 4 is a lifetime consequence of hunk 3 and travels with it.


Patch #4 -- a `transition` whose value contains var() never runs, and says nothing
(bead VaCuus-6gj).

One file, one hunk: Source/Core/ElementStyle.cpp, ElementStyle::TransitionPropertyChanges.

THE DEFECT IS UPSTREAM'S and it is silent in the strongest sense -- no warning, no error,
no log line anywhere, in a debug build, at any log level. A property value containing var()
is stored UNPARSED as Property{value, Unit::VAR_EXPRESSION} (Source/Core/
PropertySpecification.cpp:260-267) and resolved at COMPUTE time (ElementStyle.cpp:277-315).
That is deliberate and correct, and it is exactly why var() works everywhere else. But
TransitionPropertyChanges reads `transition` EARLY, on purpose -- "We get the local property
directly here to intercept property changes even before the computed values are ready"
(:388) -- and then tested `transition_property->value.GetType() != Variant::TRANSITIONLIST`
and returned. A VAR_EXPRESSION is a String variant, so it returned, and the whole
declaration was gone.

The blast radius is the obvious authoring idiom: RCSS has no calc(), so var() is the only
theming layer the matrix can recommend, and timing tokens in custom properties are the first
thing anyone does with it. In the 2d6 demo that was ~30 transitions across four component
batches, three screens and a screenshot-reviewed component catalogue, none of which had ever
run, for days, because the symptom is "the element snaps".

`animation` IS NOT AFFECTED and needs no patch, contrary to the original bug report. It is
read through ComputedValues::animation(), which goes via GetLocalPropertyWithResolvedVariables
and therefore resolves (Source/Core/ComputedValues.cpp:8-16). Measured, not assumed: with this
patch fully reverted, the test's #anim-variable element still animates.

THE HUNK is a PURE INSERTION -- `git diff` on the file reports 36 insertions and zero
deletions, deliberately, so a re-vendor can paste it back between the null check and the
TRANSITIONLIST test without touching an upstream line:

    const Property* transition_property = GetLocalProperty(PropertyId::Transition, sources.inline_properties, new_definition);
    if (!transition_property)
        return;
+   /* the full comment is in the file; not repeated here, twice is what rots */
+   Property transition_property_storage;
+   if (transition_property->unit == Unit::VAR_EXPRESSION)
+   {
+       const PropertySources transition_sources{sources.element, new_definition, sources.inline_properties};
+       std::optional<PropertyDictionary> transition_substituted_shorthands;
+       SmallUnorderedSet<String> transition_variable_dependencies;
+       transition_property = ResolveVariablesWithShorthandExpansion(transition_sources, PropertyId::Transition,
+           transition_property, transition_substituted_shorthands, transition_variable_dependencies,
+           transition_property_storage);
+       if (!transition_property)
+           return;
+   }
    if (transition_property->value.GetType() != Variant::TRANSITIONLIST)
        return;

`transition_property_storage` is what the TransitionList reference two lines down borrows,
so it must stay at function scope; the set and the optional are block-local on purpose, so
that a `transition` with no var() in it constructs neither.

WHY THIS IS SAFE HERE SPECIFICALLY, opened rather than assumed. The worry with resolving
anything at this point is compute ordering, and upstream has already answered it: the
substitution path names THIS FUNCTION as the case it is written for -- "We cannot always use
the definition or inline properties from the style of the property element. Particularly in
TransitionPropertyChanges, these are not yet set for the current element" (:227-230) -- and
this same function already calls the same helper on every transitioned property's start and
target value a few lines below (:410-414 before the patch). The sources passed here match
the lookup exactly: the element's current inline properties against the NEW definition, so a
custom property redeclared by the same rule that changed the transition resolves against the
state being transitioned TO. `transition` is a plain property, not a shorthand
(StyleSheetSpecification.cpp:399, and no RegisterShorthand under that name), so the
shorthand-expansion leg of the helper is never taken; it is used anyway because it is the
call the neighbouring lines make. A nullptr return means substitution failed, and
SubstituteVariables / ResolveVariables have already logged which variable or which value
(:212-217, :308-312) -- so the remaining failure mode is loud, which the original never was.
Cost is zero unless the property really is a VAR_EXPRESSION.

WHY THIS IS NOT FIXED AT THE VaCuus LAYER: the plugin never sees this call. TransitionProperty-
Changes is private to ElementStyle, `transition` cannot be re-registered over
(StyleSheetSpecification::RegisterParser refuses a duplicate name, :99-110), and there is no
element hook between the definition change and the early read. A VaCuus-side WARNING was
considered as the fallback deliverable and rejected once the fix landed: after this patch the
`!= TRANSITIONLIST` branch is unreachable for a var() value, so the warning would be dead
code, and the branch it would guard lives in this same function -- a re-vendor that lost the
patch would lose the warning with it. The automation test below is the guard instead.

VERIFICATION (the re-vendoring check): automation test VaCuus.Core.Style.TransitionVariable
(Source/VaCuus/Private/Tests/VaCuusStyleVariableTest.cpp). Reverted and watched to fail on
2026-08-06:

  #variable, transition with var() in its duration STARTS rather than snapping (6gj):
    expected opacity 1.0000 (±0.0100), got 0.2500
  #variable, var(--slow) = 20s, has barely moved after 250 ms:
    expected opacity 0.9500 (±0.0600), got 0.2500

with every control still passing -- including "#anim-variable, animation with var() runs too
-- it was NEVER the broken half (6gj): opacity 0.2500", which is what keeps a future reader
from patching the animation path as well.

NOT yet offered upstream -- same standing as patches #1-#3. This one is the most
upstream-shaped of the four: it uses upstream's own helper, in the function upstream's own
comment says that helper was written for.


Patch #5 -- a character no loaded face covers becomes U+FFFD with no log at any level
(bead VaCuus-sg2.6).

Seven files, all small. Four of them exist only to carry the count out to a caller.

  Source/Core/FontEngineDefault/FontFaceHandleDefault.cpp   the call site (one line)
  Source/Core/FontEngineDefault/FontProvider.h / .cpp       the counter and the warning
  Source/Core/FontEngineDefault/FontEngineInterfaceDefault.h / .cpp  the override
  Include/RmlUi/Core/FontEngineInterface.h                  the virtual, defaulted to 0
  Source/Core/FontEngineInterface.cpp                       that default

THE DEFECT IS UPSTREAM'S AND IT IS A DIAGNOSTIC HOLE, not a rendering bug -- the
substitution itself is correct behaviour. FontFaceHandleDefault::GetOrAppendGlyph, having
missed in the styled face and then in every fallback face, does this:

    // If we still have not found a glyph, use the replacement character.
    if (it_glyph == glyphs.end())
    {
        character = Character::Replacement;
        it_glyph = glyphs.find(character);
        if (it_glyph == glyphs.end())
            return nullptr;
    }

No Log::Message, no counter, nothing. So a document rendered ENTIRELY in replacement
characters is indistinguishable, from the log, from one that rendered perfectly.

WHY THAT MATTERS HERE MORE THAN IT DOES UPSTREAM. VaCuus ships exactly one face,
Content/DevUI/fonts/LatoLatin-Regular.ttf, and it is Latin-only -- measured with fc-query:
20-7e, a0-17f, plus assorted symbols. No Cyrillic, no CJK, no Greek beyond a few maths
glyphs. That is the default every buyer starts from, so the first thing a localized game
does -- push a Russian or Chinese table -- lands exactly on this path, and the buyer's
report is "the text is all boxes" with a clean log to go with it.

WHY IT IS NOT FIXED AT THE VaCuus LAYER: the plugin never sees the call. Glyph lookup
happens inside FontFaceHandleDefault during layout; FontEngineInterface has no hook near
it, and the only VaCuus-visible surface (FVaCuusSystemInterface::LogMessage) can report
what RmlUi decides to say -- which is nothing. Replacing the whole font engine to obtain
one counter is not a proportionate answer.

THE SHAPE, chosen to be upstreamable rather than convenient: a virtual on the public
FontEngineInterface with a base implementation returning 0, overridden by the default
engine. An engine that cannot report this answers "0 substitutions", which is why the
API is a COUNT and not a bool -- "cannot say" and "nothing wrong" must not be the same
value by construction, and a count makes the difference visible in the trend rather than
in the type. The warning is latched to ONE line per RmlUi initialisation because this
runs inside text layout; a line per glyph would flood at frame rate. Both the counter and
the latch are instance members of FontProvider, so they reset when Rml::Initialise
recreates it -- the same lifetime as the face list beside them.

VERIFICATION (the re-vendoring check): automation test VaCuus.Font.MissingGlyph
(Source/VaCuus/Private/Tests/VaCuusFontRegistryTest.cpp). It lays out Latin text, asserts
the counter does not move across repeated frames -- the control, without which the claim
would pass on a counter that incremented on every glyph -- then loads Cyrillic and asserts
it does. Reverted (the one line at the call site commented out) and watched to fail on
2026-08-09:

  Expected 'uncovered text is COUNTED instead of silently becoming U+FFFD' to be true.

with the control still passing. Restored, green. The run also prints the new warning, which
is the other half of the deliverable:

  LogVaCuus: Warning: [Rml] No glyph for U+0417 in the styled font face or any fallback
  face; it renders as the replacement character. ...

U+0417 is the first character of the test's string, which is what says the latch reports the
FIRST offender rather than an arbitrary one.

NOT ASSERTED, and deliberately: that the count stays flat once a covering face is
registered. The repository ships one .ttf and it has no Cyrillic, so there is no face to
register -- proving that half needs a font asset, which is a licensing decision.

NOT yet offered upstream -- same standing as patches #1-#4. This one is worth offering on
its own merits even to a project that never uses VaCuus: it costs an int, changes no
rendering behaviour, and turns a class of silent failure into a one-line warning.


Patch #6 -- two data-binding headers leave DataExpression incomplete where libc++ 18
instantiates the unique_ptr deleter (bead VaCuus-3nl, the first Android compile).

Source/Core/DataViewDefault.h and Source/Core/DataControllerDefault.h each hold a
`DataExpressionPtr` member (a `UniquePtr<DataExpression>`) behind a forward
declaration only, relying on every includer instantiating the implicit destructor
in a TU that has seen the full type. Desktop toolchains here (clang 20/Linux,
Apple clang/Metal, MSVC) happened to satisfy that through their unity groupings.
The NDK r27c libc++ (18.x) does not: its unique_ptr destructor is
_LIBCPP_CONSTEXPR_SINCE_CXX23, and in the Android unity blob for Factory.cpp the
deleter is instantiated with the type still incomplete --
`static_assert(sizeof(_Tp) >= 0, "cannot delete an incomplete type")`
(__memory/unique_ptr.h:64) fails the build.

THE HUNK, same one line in both files: add `#include "DataExpression.h"` (the
private header in the same directory) so the type is complete for every includer.
No behavioural change; the forward declarations stay, now redundant but harmless.

VERIFICATION (the re-vendoring check): the Android compile itself.
`Mac/Build.sh TP_ThirdPerson Android Development -project=<VcHost> -NoXGE` on the
Mac fails without the includes exactly as above (va-macbook
~/VaCuusSession-android/build1.log, 2026-08-11) and is green with them
(build3.log, same day). Desktop targets cannot see this defect either way.

NOT yet offered upstream -- same standing as patches #1-#5. Checked against
mikke89/RmlUi master 2026-08-11: both headers still carry the forward-declaration-
only pattern, so the defect is live upstream for any strict-libc++ consumer.


Patch #7 -- a transformed stacking context never re-dirties elements that join it later.
Backport of upstream mikke89/RmlUi 6df503c; EXPIRES at the first re-vendor at or after
it (bead VaCuus-74s).

Applied 2026-09-14 from PR #2, ahead of our own next re-vendor, with the corrections of
bead VaCuus-kga. Element.cpp line numbers in this entry and in its test are for THIS
tree, with the hunk applied; upstream's pre-patch numbers are 7 lower from line 2380 on.

Symptom: an element that becomes visible underneath an ancestor with its own
`transform` renders unscaled -- full size, at its untransformed layout position --
instead of picking up the ancestor's resolved matrix. A VaCuus document hits this
whenever a `data-if` (inline `display: none`, DataViewDefault.cpp:264-266) flips true
inside a panel whose transform already resolved; and, by a second route, whenever a
`data-for` clone is created inside such a panel: the clone's own box scales, the
content filled into it does not. The same missing state breaks hit-testing for those
elements too: the interactive snapshot gates its projected path on GetTransformState()
(Source/VaCuusRender/Private/VaCuusInteractiveSnapshot.cpp:499), so the untransformed
rect is what the game thread hit-tests -- consistently wrong on both channels.

Cause, in this vendored tree:
- The only way a member of a transformed stacking context gets its matrix is the
  propagation loop at the end of `Element::UpdateTransformState`
  (Element.cpp:3037-3041): it runs over the CURRENT `stacking_context` members, and
  only when the container's matrix actually CHANGED in this render
  (`perspective_or_transform_changed`, :3037). It is not gated by the dirty flag.
  `dirty_transform` is sticky -- the only write is the `|=` at :2892, with no
  `= false` twin of the perspective reset at :2953 -- so a container that ever held a
  matrix recomputes its (unchanged) matrix on every render for life, propagating
  nothing, and the early-out at :2897 is only ever taken by an element that has NEVER
  been dirtied. Dirtying the container from the visibility path is therefore not an
  alternative fix: it is already dirty.
- `AddToStackingContext` skips invisible elements (Element.cpp:2397-2398), and
  `visible` is false under `display: none` and `visibility: hidden` alike (:1856-1857),
  so a hidden element was not a member while the container's matrix resolved, and the
  one propagation that would have reached it has already happened.
- `SetParent` dirties a newly-parented element only when it or its NEW PARENT already
  holds a transform_state (Element.cpp:2190-2192). Every rendered member of a
  transformed subtree holds one (:3002-3028 copies the stacking parent's matrix into
  each member's own state), so a leaf inserted under a rendered member IS dirtied and
  renders correctly without this patch -- that is not the bug, and a test that inserts
  a leaf passes with the hunk reverted (AfterLateInsert keeps one as its control). The
  insert that fails is content under a parent that has not rendered yet, which is what
  DataViewFor::Update does to every clone: InsertBefore (DataViewDefault.cpp:563;
  dirtied, its parent has a state) and then SetInnerRML (:567) while the clone's own
  state is still null, so the content is parented without a dirty. The clone's first
  render then propagates over ITS `stacking_context`, which is empty because a plain
  block is not a stacking-context container -- the content lives in the CONTAINER's
  flat list -- and the content renders under identity.
- `BuildLocalStackingContext` rebuilds the flat member list on every DOM insert/remove
  and every display/visibility/z-index change (`DirtyStackingContext` marks the closest
  container, Element.cpp:2489-2493) without dirtying anyone (:2362-2372, the body
  before the hunk), and is reached from two places: `Element::Render` (:188-189, before
  that element's own UpdateTransformState at :191) and `Context::GetElementAtPoint`
  (Context.cpp:1407-1408, the hover and input paths, during Update).
So an element that joins the container's stacking context after the container's matrix
last changed is added to the list and never told to compute -- it keeps whatever state
it had, which for a hidden-from-birth or freshly-created element is none, i.e. identity.
The reverse direction self-heals: an element that once held a matrix stays dirty and
recomputes each render, which is also why the hunk's one-directional guard is enough.

The change: `Element::BuildLocalStackingContext` (:2373-2379) now dirties every member
of the freshly-rebuilt list whenever the container itself holds a transform_state --

	// If the stacking context changed, any previously hidden elements may not have had their transforms updated. Ensure they will be updated now.
	if (transform_state)
	{
		for (Element* child : stacking_context)
			child->DirtyTransformState(false, true);
	}

Upstream reference: mikke89/RmlUi commit 6df503c (2026-08-16), "Fix transform not
being applied after element turns visible, see #982". The Element.cpp hunk here is
byte-identical to upstream's. The rest of that commit is a comment typo in
TransformState.h and doctest support under Tests/, which this tree does not vendor
(see "What is here, and why exactly this" above); the doctest is ported as an
automation test instead, below.

Cost: no element changes cost class. Every member that already rendered correctly was
already sticky-dirty and recomputing every render; the loop only adds the previously
wrong-rendering members to that set, at one bool OR per member per rebuild. The rebuild
runs only while `stacking_context_dirty` is set, not every frame, but the list it walks
is the FLAT one (AddChildrenToStackingContext recurses through every descendant that is
not itself a stacking-context container), so a rebuild of a large transformed panel
touches all of its descendants. The GetElementAtPoint rebuild can run the loop during
Update; that only sets flags -- matrices are computed in Render, after layout -- so it
is benign.

One-frame consequence for VaCuus, noted so nobody files it as a regression: the
interactive snapshot is built between Update() and Render()
(Source/VaCuusRender/Private/VaCuusRmlDocumentHost.cpp:640-672), and the newly-shown
element's transform_state appears in that frame's Render, so on the reveal frame the
snapshot hit-tests the untransformed rect and converges on the next. It is the same lag
any transform property change already has (OnPropertyChange dirties,
Element.cpp:1962-1963; Render computes). Before this patch the two channels were
wrong-but-consistent forever.

VERIFICATION (the re-vendoring check): two automation tests in
Source/VaCuusRender/Private/Tests/VaCuusTransformVisibilityTest.cpp, both reading the
recorded RenderInterface::SetTransform stream (FVaCuusRecordingRenderInterface) -- the
file header says why that seam and not GetTransformState(). Each has a positive control
(an always-visible reference pane, seen to draw under a non-identity matrix) and
compares every target against the reference's recorded matrix in the same frame.
- VaCuus.Render.Transform.AfterVisibilityChange, the port of upstream's doctest
  `Element.TransformStateAfterVisibilityChange` with both of its SUBCASEs:
  `#window { transform: scale(2) }` holds the reference, a `display: none` pane and a
  `visibility: hidden` pane; one frame after the scale resolved both are shown and
  must draw under the reference's matrix.
- VaCuus.Render.Transform.AfterLateInsert, the data-for shape: after frame 1 a leaf is
  appended straight under #window (the control -- correct with or without the hunk,
  see the SetParent bullet) and a wrapper is appended and then filled with SetInnerRML;
  the nested pane must draw under the reference's matrix.
Restore-the-bug, Linux clang, 2026-09-14, with ONLY the Element.cpp hunk reverted and
the tests unchanged: AfterVisibilityChange fails exactly its four matrix assertions
("draws under pane_reference's matrix" and "draws under a non-identity transform", for
pane_display and for pane_visibility); AfterLateInsert fails exactly the same two for
pane_nested while both of pane_direct's hold; every positive control and every "does
not draw while hidden" check still passes. Hunk restored: both Success. The PR author
saw the display case fail and pass the same way on UE 5.8 Win64.

Drop this patch when RmlUi is re-vendored at or after 6df503c. Reapplying it on top of
an upstream tree that already carries it doubles the loop with nothing to flag it:
DirtyTransformState is an idempotent OR (Element.cpp:2891-2892) and both tests pass
either way. Diff the re-vendored BuildLocalStackingContext against the hunk first, in
case the upstream form has moved, then remove this entry (bead VaCuus-74s).


Patch #8 -- a shrinking `data-for` evaluates the rows it is about to remove.

One file, one hunk: Source/Core/DataViewDefault.cpp, DataViewFor's constructor passes a sort bias
of -1000 instead of 0.

THE HUNK'S COMMENT IS SEVEN LINES, so DataViewDefault.cpp line numbers from 448 on are seven
higher in this tree than upstream's and than any citation written before this patch -- the same
shape as patch #7's Element.cpp shift, and the reason that entry carries the same note. Patch #7
cites this file twice; both were renumbered with this patch (:544 -> :551, :548 -> :555), in its
entry above and in its test. Citations elsewhere in the tree were left as they stand, exactly as
patch #7's shift left its own -- bead VaCuus-8sg carries that, for both patches at once.

THE DEFECT IS UPSTREAM'S, and it is live on mikke89/RmlUi master (checked 2026-09-17: DataViewFor
still passes 0, and DataView.cpp has had only formatting and license-header commits since fb2351d,
2021, which introduced the biases). Symptom: a shrink of an array whose `data-for` row element
carries bindings of its own --

    <div data-for="r : Replies" data-attr-reply="r.Id" data-class-is-played="r.bPlayed">

-- logs "Could not get value from data variable 'Replies[2].Id'." for some or all of the removed
rows, varying from one shrink to the next. The rows that remain render correctly. The warnings are
the whole symptom: each one is a read past the end of the shrunk array. Found in a game's dialogue
window, where every click on a reply shrinks the list of replies.

Cause, in this tree (line numbers WITH the hunk applied):
- DataViews::Update sorts the dirty views by GetSortOrder alone (Source/Core/DataView.cpp:104), and
  the sort order is `bias + 1000 + 2000 * depth`, fixed when the view is constructed
  (DataView.cpp:27-36). The comment above the sort gives the intent -- "the 'data-for' view will
  remove children if any of its data variable array size is reduced" (:102-103) -- but the rows are
  not its children. DataViewFor::Update inserts every row as a SIBLING, before the template element
  (DataViewDefault.cpp:563).
- A row's views are constructed when the row is parented: SetParent sets `parent` (Element.cpp:2181)
  and then calls SetDataModel (:2206), which runs ApplyDataViewsControllers (:2162). By then the row
  is already at the template's depth. A row carries the template's attributes minus `data-for`
  (DataViewDefault.cpp:526-531), so its data-attr, data-class, data-if and so on are views on the row
  element itself, at the depth of the data-for view. Their bias is 0 (DataViewDefault.cpp:22, through
  :60 and :203) or higher (data-value 100 and data-checked 110, :17 and :19). The data-for view's
  bias was 0 as well.
- So the data-for view and the row views with bias 0 share one sort key. Every row view is dirty
  whenever the array is, because an aliased `r.Id` reduces to the root name `Replies`
  (DataExpression.cpp:1146-1156). std::sort keeps equal keys in no defined order, and the sort
  before it orders the views by pointer value (DataView.cpp:98), so which one runs first depends on
  heap addresses. A row view that runs after the data-for view finds its element already
  destroyed (the RemoveChild(...).reset() at DataViewDefault.cpp:574) and is skipped
  (DataView.cpp:112). A row view that runs BEFORE it evaluates `Replies[2]` against the shrunk array,
  gets an empty variable back from DataModel::GetVariable (DataModel.cpp:285-290), and logs the
  warning (DataModel.cpp:321).

The change: DataViewFor passes the lowest bias the constructor's assert allows (DataView.cpp:29).
Its sort order becomes `2000 * depth`. That is below every non-structural view at its own depth
(bias >= 0, so >= 1000 + 2000 * depth) and still above every view of its parent (at most
1999 + 2000 * (depth - 1)). Rows are now removed before any row view runs. Growth is unaffected:
the new rows' views are new views, and they run in the next round of the same Update
(DataView.cpp:70-87), exactly as before.

Cost: none added. The dirty set is the same. The only evaluations that change are those of a
removed row's views, which are now skipped every time instead of only when the sort placed them
after the data-for view.

WHY THIS IS NOT FIXED AT THE VaCuus LAYER: the plugin never sees the order. It is local to
DataViews::Update, and "for" cannot be replaced with a differently biased instancer:
Factory::RegisterDataViewInstancer refuses a name that is already registered
(Source/Core/Factory.cpp:563-567), and "for" is registered at start-up (:247). A document can avoid
the defect by moving the bindings onto a child of the row element, one level deeper, but that is a
rule every document author would have to know, for a warning whose cause is not visible in the
document.

VERIFICATION (the re-vendoring check): automation test VaCuus.Core.DataFor.ShrinkOrder
(Source/VaCuus/Private/Tests/VaCuusDataForOrderTest.cpp). It binds a counting array definition
under a `data-for` row element with three bindings, runs a walk of grows and shrinks that removes
2910 row views, and asserts that no shrink reads a row past the end. Its controls check that every
row shows its own values after every step, and that the surviving rows' views were evaluated in each
shrink's update.
Restore-the-bug, Win64, UE 5.8.1 DebugGame host editor, -unattended -nullrhi, 2026-09-17:
  - hunk reverted: Result={Fail} in three runs out of three, and only the six "no row view read
    past the end of the array" assertions fail; every control passes. Per shrink, the reads past
    the end were 18 of the 18 row views removed, 177 of 177, 768 of 768, 297 of 297, 450 of 450,
    and 876, 1080 and 794 of 1200 in the three runs.
  - hunk restored: Success, "2910 row views removed across the walk, 0 reads past the end, 3432
    in range".

NOT yet offered upstream -- same standing as patches #1-#6.

Patch #9 -- text-transform changes the case of ASCII letters only.

One file: Source/Core/ElementText.cpp. The old BuildToken body becomes BuildTokenUntransformed
(:580, same logic, the transform parameter and the ASCII-only transform block removed), and a new
BuildToken with the old signature (:818) calls it and then, for Uppercase or Lowercase, re-encodes
the token code point by code point (TransformTextCase, :794). The forward declaration (:21) and both
call sites in GenerateLine (:265, :308) are untouched.

THE DEFECT IS UPSTREAM'S. BuildToken walks the UTF-8 text one BYTE at a time
(`char character = *token_begin;`) and applied the transform only to `a-z` / `A-Z` (pre-patch
:679-688). A multi-byte code point never matches, so `text-transform: uppercase` renders "Accept"
as ACCEPT but a Russian, Greek, Spanish or French caption unchanged. Found in a game localised into
Russian: ten RCSS rules (captions, buttons, toast and tracker titles, speaker names) put English in
capitals and left every Russian string in mixed case. Only the letters of the string's own ASCII
runs change -- "nandu" with n-tilde and u-acute comes out as n-tilde + "AND" + u-acute.

The mapping (ToUpperCharacter :711, ToLowerCharacter :745) is Unicode's simple, one-to-one case
mapping (UnicodeData.txt fields 12 and 13) for ASCII, Latin-1 Supplement, Latin Extended-A, Latin
Extended Additional, Greek and Cyrillic + Cyrillic Supplement: the contiguous blocks by offset, the
even/odd pair blocks by parity, and the irregular letters (y-diaeresis / Y-diaeresis, dotted
capital I, dotless i, long s, final sigma, the Greek tonos letters, palochka, capital sharp s) by
name. Everything else, and letters whose other case needs two code points (German sharp s), keeps
its case -- as all of it did before. `capitalize` stays unimplemented, as it was.

Only a well-formed code point is re-encoded: one whose span to the next lead byte equals its own
canonical encoding. SeekForwardUTF8 skips every continuation byte whatever the lead byte declared
(Include/RmlUi/Core/StringUtilities.h:100-105) while ToCharacter reads only the declared count and
returns Null for a bad lead, a truncated or a broken sequence (Source/Core/StringUtilities.cpp:
431-478), so without that check an orphan continuation byte after a letter would be swallowed on
re-encoding. A bad lead, a truncated or overlong sequence and orphan continuation bytes are copied
byte for byte, as before. That branch holds by construction and review, not by test: a document
built from FString text cannot carry malformed UTF-8.

Cost: GenerateLine runs at layout (Layout/InlineLevelBox.cpp:154, Elements/WidgetTextInput.cpp:
1291), not per frame, and only elements with text-transform uppercase or lowercase take the second
pass; `none` returns straight after BuildTokenUntransformed.

Test: VaCuus.Rml.TextTransform.Unicode (Source/VaCuus/Private/Tests/VaCuusTextTransformTest.cpp)
lays out an uppercase, a lowercase and an untransformed div -- Latin, Cyrillic, Greek, Latin-1,
sharp s, dotless and dotted I -- and compares each ElementText's GetLines() text, the string before
glyph lookup, so the LatoLatin face need not cover Cyrillic or Greek. The source file stays ASCII:
every non-ASCII letter is built from its code point at run time.
Restore-the-bug, Win64, UE 5.8 host editor, -unattended -nullrhi, 2026-09-26:
  - patch absent: Result={Fail} on "upper" and "lower" only -- the uppercase div read back as
    "ACCEPT" + the Cyrillic, Greek and accented letters unchanged + "STRA" sharp-s "E" + dotless i;
    the untransformed control passed;
  - patch present: Success; the rest of VaCuus. green alongside it (447 of 447 with the host's own
    UI tests).

NOT yet offered upstream -- same standing as patches #1-#6 and #8.

Patch #9 follow-up (owner, landing PR #19) -- the text-input widget must stay untransformed.
Four mappings change a letter's UTF-8 length (dotless i -> I, dotted capital I -> i, long s ->
S, capital sharp s -> sharp s). WidgetTextInput takes the displayed line's byte count as a
length in its value (Source/Core/Elements/WidgetTextInput.cpp:1294, used at :873 and :1098),
so a transformed field would misplace its cursor. It is safe only because the widget pins
`text-transform: none` on its element (:169), which neither inheritance nor the element's own
style attribute overrides. VaCuus.Rml.TextTransform.InputByteParity guards that line: with :169
removed it fails -- End in an uppercase "kap" + dotless i field snaps back before the dotless i
and the typed 'x' lands inside the word; with :169 present it passes. A re-vendor that drops
:169 must make the transform length-preserving on that path instead.

Patch #10 -- a write the data model delivered elsewhere is not a failed assignment (bead VaCuus-w87.1).

Three files. Include/RmlUi/Core/DataVariable.h gives VariableDefinition three statics (:59-69):
public ResetAssignmentDelivered and ConsumeAssignmentDelivered, protected MarkAssignmentDelivered.
Source/Core/DataVariable.cpp defines them over one plain static flag at the end of the file
(:171-189). Source/Core/DataExpression.cpp's Assign instruction resets the flag, runs the
assignment, and reports "Could not assign to variable." only when Set() returned false AND the flag
was not set (:1070-1072).

THE DEFECT IS THE CONTRACT'S, NOT UPSTREAM'S CODE. RmlUi reads a false Set() as "the assignment
failed" and, separately, as "do not dirty the variable" -- both call sites skip DirtyVariable on
false (DataExpression.cpp:1192-1195 in SetValue, DataControllerDefault.cpp:57-59). VaCuus's write
router needs the second without the first: FVaCuusScalarDefinition::Set hands the value to the game
thread and returns false so the UI shadow is never written (invariant I3). The Assign path then
logged "Error during execution. Could not assign to variable.", "Failed to execute program with N
instructions:" and a program dump on EVERY correct data-event-click -- 27 Warning lines in one
six-minute session in the 2026-10-06 field report, which broke ai-guide.md's rule that a clean
LogVaCuus is evidence. The change-controller path (data-checked, data-value) never logged.

Reset before, consume after: a stale mark from a change-controller Set, which nobody consumes, can
never excuse a later assignment that fails before reaching Set (an address GetVariable cannot
resolve). The REFUSAL path in FVaCuusScalarDefinition::Set does not mark, so a write nobody received
keeps RmlUi's line.

Line shifts: DataVariable.h +5 from :59 and +9 from old :62; DataExpression.cpp +1 from old :1071.
Every in-repo citation into either file was moved by that map, each one checked by comparing the
HEAD line with the shifted current line (all equal); docs/research notes were left as dated records.

Tests: VaCuus.Js.Router.WriteRoutesAndReverts asserts zero "Could not assign to variable" and zero
"Failed to execute program" lines over its routed clicks; VaCuus.Model.ArrayBinding asserts exactly
2 over its two REFUSED clicks. Restore-the-bug, Linux, UE 5.8 source editor, -nullrhi, 2026-10-06:
patch absent -> the router test reads 2 and 2 (Fail); patch present -> both pass, ArrayBinding
passes either way.

Patch #11 -- a data-for alias that a top-level variable shadows is an Error naming element and document (bead VaCuus-w87.5).

Two files. Source/Core/DataViewDefault.cpp: DataViewFor::Initialize checks the iterator and index
aliases against the model's top-level variables and logs LT_ERROR once per data-for, with the
template's address and its document's source URL (:501-506). Source/Core/DataModel.cpp:
InsertAlias's generic LT_WARNING ("Alias variable '%s' is shadowed by a global variable.") becomes
the same LT_ERROR, reported only for an element that is already placed -- the data-alias path --
because a data-for row is inserted BEFORE it is parented (DataViewDefault.cpp:560-563) and has no
address or document to name (:191-192, edited in place). Both files now include ElementDocument.h
IN PLACE OF Element.h (which it includes) for GetSourceURL, so neither include block grew a line.

THE DEFECT: DataModel::ResolveAddress tries the top-level variables before any alias
(DataModel.cpp:234-236), so a shadowed alias is unreachable. Every VaCuus model binds the
translation variable `t`, and `data-for="t : Traits"` printed the key fallback "Text" on every card
of a shipped-looking screen while the only diagnostic named neither document nor element.

Line shifts: DataViewDefault.cpp +7 from old :496 (on top of patch #12's +5 from :190); DataModel.cpp
none. Test: VaCuus.Model.AliasShadowed (VaCuusBindDiagnosticsTest.cpp) -- one Error per data-for for
`t` and for an ordinary field name, naming `div < div#trows < body` and the document URL, and zero
of RmlUi's old generic Warning. Seen red before the patch (Fail: no Error, 4 generic Warnings).

Patch #12 -- an empty string in a data-style binding unsets the property; the parse Warning names the element (bead VaCuus-w87.8).

Two files. Source/Core/DataViewDefault.cpp, DataViewStyle::Update -- patch #1's function -- gains
an empty-value branch that calls Element::RemoveProperty (:189-193): CSSOM's `style.color = ''`
semantics. Source/Core/Element.cpp's "Syntax error parsing inline property declaration" Warning
gains " on <element address>" (:597, edited in place, no shift).

THE DEFECT: an empty bound string was handed to SetProperty, failed to parse, warned with no
element named, and repeated on every update of the variable -- and bindings under a false data-if
keep evaluating (data-if only writes display:none), so a HIDDEN card with default-constructed
colour fields produced the noise with nothing on screen to explain it. Worse than noise: returning
a field to "" left the previous colour in place.

Line shifts: DataViewDefault.cpp +5 from old :190. Test: VaCuus.Model.EmptyStyleValue -- "" sets
nothing and warns nothing; a colour then "" again removes it; a malformed value still warns, now with
`div#swatch`. Seen red before the patch (one parse Warning per empty write; the stale colour stayed).

Patch #13 -- a font weight no face of the family has is reported once (bead VaCuus-w87.13).

Two files. Source/Core/FontEngineDefault/FontFamily.h gives FontFamily a set of reported
(style, weight) misses (:42-43); FontFamily.cpp's GetFaceHandle logs one LT_WARNING per miss when
the face it chose has a different weight from the one asked for (:50-54), and includes Log.h (:3).

THE DEFECT: GetFaceHandle silently draws the nearest weight. VaCuus ships one face, LatoLatin-Regular,
so every `font-weight: bold` rule draws regular with nothing logged. Owner decision 2026-10-06: a
Warning, no bold face shipped. The test is the chosen face's weight, not the loop's best distance --
a non-matching face met BEFORE an exact match leaves the distance finite, and testing it reported a
miss that was not one (caught in review before the first build).

Line shifts: FontFamily.h +3 from old :42; FontFamily.cpp +1 from :3 and +6 from old :48; no in-repo
citations into either file existed. Test: VaCuus.Font.MissingWeight -- two bold paragraphs, one
Warning. Restore-the-bug, 2026-10-06: Warning removed -> expectation unmet (Fail); latch removed ->
"found 2 time(s)" (Fail); both present -> pass.

NOT yet offered upstream, any of #10-#13. #11, #12 and #13 are upstream-shaped as they stand; #10
exists for a write router upstream does not have, and would need a reason to be accepted.

Patch #14 -- a fractional font-size loads the face one whole pixel below it.

One file, one hunk: Source/Core/ElementStyle.cpp, ElementStyle::ComputeValues asks the font engine
for the face at Math::RoundToInteger(font_size) instead of (int)font_size (:1035-1038).

THE DEFECT IS UPSTREAM'S. The font engine keys a face by a whole pixel size
(Include/RmlUi/Core/FontEngineInterface.h:68), and the computed font-size is a float that is whole
only when it was authored in px: dp is the number times the context's ratio
(Source/Core/ComputeProperty.cpp:62), which VaCuus sets per view (VaCuusUIThread.cpp:1716-1720),
and em, rem, vw and vh scale the same way. The cast always went down, so a size a hair under a
pixel lost the whole pixel -- 10.95px drew at 10, 13dp at a ratio of 1.5 (19.5px) at 19 -- while
the line height, computed from the float, kept the full size. Found in a game that sets
`body { font-size: 0.0925926vh; }` so its UI scales with the window: below 1080 high nearly every
size is fractional, and each caption drew up to a pixel small.

Math::RoundToInteger rounds half away from zero (Source/Core/Math.cpp:121-127), so 10.5 is 11.
This is the only place Source/Core turns a computed font-size into a face size; every other
GetFontFaceHandle in it is Element's accessor for the handle stored here.

Line shifts: ElementStyle.cpp +2 from old :1037. Two in-repo citations moved, each compared with
the line it named on master (equal): this file's (ElementStyle.cpp:1060-1064, top of the file) and
docs/buyer/gotchas.md (:1249). Dated design notes under docs/superpowers were left as records.

Test: VaCuus.Font.FractionalSize (Source/VaCuus/Private/Tests/VaCuusFontSizeTest.cpp) -- divs at
10.95px, 10.5px and 13dp with the context's dp ratio at 1.5, and two controls at 10.4px and 11px;
it reads the size of the face each one's computed values hold, through
FontEngineInterface::GetFontMetrics. Restore-the-bug, Win64, UE 5.8 host editor, -unattended
-nullrhi, 2026-10-16:
  - patch absent: Result={Fail} on the three fractional divs only -- faces of 10, 10 and 19 px
    against 11, 11 and 20; both controls passed;
  - patch present: Success; the rest of VaCuus. green alongside it (280 of 280).

NOT yet offered upstream. Upstream-shaped as it stands.

Patch #15 -- text is laid out on whole pixels, so small type spaces unevenly and drops its tracking.

Files: Include/RmlUi/Core/FontGlyph.h (advance_exact :17-19, and WeakCopy carrying it :36 -- a
fallback-face glyph without it advances by 0 and the next glyph lands on top of it),
Source/Core/FontEngineDefault/FreeTypeInterface.h/.cpp (GetKerning :214-241, the replacement glyph
:272, BuildGlyph and its bitmap-strike scaling :340-344 and :354), FontFaceHandleDefault.h/.cpp (the
Math.h include, StringWidthToPixels :18-24, GetStringWidth :68-96, GenerateString :181-258, the
kerning cache and its value type, GetKerning), FontFaceLayer.h (the Math.h include, GenerateGeometry
:59-78), Source/Core/ElementText.cpp (GenerateLine, the two token measurements :262-265 and :303-304),
Source/Core/Elements/WidgetTextInput.cpp (FormatText, the trailing spaces :1308). Every hunk of this
patch, at git's default three lines of context, carries "VaCuus patch #15": grep for it, and expect
it on includes and one-word type changes too.

Symptom: a root font-size in vh (a game's `body { font-size: 0.0925926vh; }`, so its UI scales with
the window) makes every length fractional below 1080 high. An 11 px caption reads "INT ERACT IVE":
neighbouring gaps differ by up to a pixel and a half where the face meant them equal; 0.12em of
tracking on 9 px type vanishes; -0.05em never applies.

Cause, upstream behaviour at the pinned SHA (pre-patch lines):
- a glyph advances by `metrics.horiAdvance >> 6` (FreeTypeInterface.cpp:336, BuildGlyph). The glyph
  is loaded hinted (:296, FT_LOAD_COLOR alone), so FreeType has already grid-fitted that advance to
  a whole pixel (FreeType 2.14.1 src/base/ftobjs.c:889, called at :1079-1081);
- `letter_spacing` is cast to int per glyph (FontFaceHandleDefault.cpp:80 in GetStringWidth, :239
  in GenerateString), so anything under a pixel is 0;
- kerning is FT_KERNING_DEFAULT shifted down (FreeTypeInterface.cpp:232-237, GetKerning). DEFAULT
  already returns whole pixels: below 25 ppem it scales the pair by ppem/25, then rounds it to the
  nearest pixel with FT_PIX_ROUND (FreeType 2.14.1 src/base/ftobjs.c:3630-3646, FT_Get_Kerning; the
  macro is include/freetype/internal/ftobjs.h:91-92). UE 5.8 ships FreeType2-2.14.1 as headers and
  libraries only, so the .c files cited here are upstream's tag VER-2-14-1. A pair under half a
  pixel after that scaling was 0, and 9-13 px type was kerned at 36-52 % of the face's value before
  the rounding;
- the quad is placed at `(position + box.origin).Round()` (FontFaceLayer.h:57, GenerateGeometry).
Computed from a game's ScienceGothic-SemiBold tables for "INTERACTIVE" at 10.95 px (drawn at the 10 px
face patch #14 fixes): the ink gap per pair against the face's own (float advances, GPOS kerning,
-0.05em) is off by -0.06 .. +0.95 px.
Rounding each glyph's origin from a float pen instead was tried on paper and is no better (worse at
13 px): only a fractional placement gives the designed gaps.

The fix: the pen runs in float -- advance_exact from linearHoriAdvance, the unhinted advance in
16.16 (FreeType's freetype.h:2106-2110), UNFITTED kerning in 26.6, the spacing as given. A glyph on
a fraction keeps its quad on the grid one pixel wider, with its texture coordinates moved left by
the fraction, and the bilinear sampler of VaCuus's textured draws (VaCuusReplayRenderer.cpp:1208)
shifts the bitmap by exactly that. The extra column reads the transparent pixel the atlas keeps
around every glyph: a row starts at x 2 and leaves two pixels after each rectangle
(Source/Core/TextureLayoutRow.cpp:19, :53; two since the follow-up below), and the atlas starts transparent
(Source/Core/TextureLayoutTexture.cpp:113-114). GetStringWidth/GenerateString still answer in
whole pixels: up, less 0.001, so a box sized to its text never clips it and float noise on a
whole sum does not add a pixel.

UNFITTED also drops DEFAULT's small-size damping: below 25 ppem a pair now gets the face's full
value, up to 25/ppem of what DEFAULT gave before rounding (2.8x at 9 px). Kerning is on unless
`font-kerning: none` (FontFaceHandleDefault.cpp:355-358), so this shows by default. Only faces with
a `kern` table are touched -- this FreeType reads no GPOS kerning (TT_CONFIG_OPTION_GPOS_KERNING is
off, FreeType2-2.14.1 include/freetype/config/ftoption.h:798; FT_FACE_FLAG_KERNING comes from `kern`
alone, sfobjs.c:1133-1138). The shipped LatoLatin has one (10920 pairs), so its small text kerns
tighter than before, by the face's own amounts.

Measuring a line (ElementText.cpp, GenerateLine): rounding every GetStringWidth up made the sum of
a line's token widths run past what GenerateString draws by up to a pixel per token -- centred and
right-aligned text sat off, a box sized to its text grew a tail, a line wrapped early. A token is
now costed as W(line + token) - W(line), W being GetStringWidth from the line's start and W(line)
the width the loop already holds, so a line measures exactly what GenerateString returns for it;
the price is re-measuring the line so far once per token. WidgetTextInput::FormatText re-measures a
line after appending its trailing spaces instead of adding a rounded-up space per space. Left as
they are: separate runs are placed at whole-pixel widths -- inline boxes on one line
(Layout/LineBox.cpp:78) and WidgetTextInput's selected, unselected and IME runs -- so each boundary
can shift the run after it by up to a pixel (placing it exactly needs a fractional width, i.e. a new
FontEngineInterface entry); and `cols`/`size` x W("m") in ElementFormControlTextArea/InputTypeText
is a size hint, at most a pixel per column wide, never narrow.

Cost: a glyph off the grid is resampled, a little softer than one on it. Kerning from GPOS (faces
with no `kern` table) is still not read -- that needs a shaper, separate work. Line breaking
measures tokens x line length per line instead of the line's length once.

Line shifts: FontFaceHandleDefault.cpp +1 from old :2, +9 from old :17, +10 from old :81, +11 from
old :240; FreeTypeInterface.cpp +3 from old :231, +2 from old :239, +3 from old :270, +8 from old
:337, +9 from old :346; FontFaceLayer.h +1 from old :6, +21 from old :58; FontGlyph.h +3 from old
:17, +4 from old :33; ElementText.cpp -4 from old :262, -1 from old :267, 0 from old :305;
FreeTypeInterface.h +1 from old :36; FontFaceHandleDefault.h and WidgetTextInput.cpp in place.
Moved in-repo citations, each compared with the line it named on master (equal):
FontFaceHandleDefault.cpp:378-394 (was :367-383) in VaCuusFontRegistry.cpp, VaCuusUIQueues.h and
VaCuusFontRegistry.h; :397-404 (was :386-393) in VaCuusFontRegistryTest.cpp, VaCuusFontRegistry.h
and VaCuusSubsystem.h; patch #9's GenerateLine call sites above, :260 and :301 (were :264, :302).
Dated design notes under docs/superpowers were left as records.

VERIFICATION (the re-vendoring check): seven automation tests in
Source/VaCuus/Private/Tests/VaCuusFontSubpixelTest.cpp, on LatoLatin through the public
FontEngineInterface:
  - VaCuus.Font.Subpixel.LetterSpacing: 0.5 px of spacing over the eleven glyphs of "INTERACTIVE",
    kerning off, adds 5 or 6 px to GetStringWidth.
  - VaCuus.Font.Subpixel.FractionalPen: GenerateString of "H" with its pen moved by 0.25, 0.5 and
    0.75 px moves the glyph by exactly that, read back from the quad's x and its texture coordinates.
  - VaCuus.Font.Subpixel.LineWidth: GenerateLine's width of a twelve-word line at 0.37 px of
    letter-spacing equals what GenerateString returns for it. Its control asks that the tokens
    measured one by one sum to more, so the text can tell the two apart.
  - VaCuus.Font.Subpixel.Advance: a hundred H at 16 px measure 1222 (1527/2000 em each, LatoLatin's
    hmtx).
  - VaCuus.Font.Subpixel.Kerning: twenty "To" kern at 10 px by their kerning at 50 px times 10/50;
    its control asks that the run kerns at 50 px at all.
  - VaCuus.Font.Subpixel.FallbackAdvance: a ZHE taken from a fallback face adds its own width between
    two A. The fallback is the engine's Engine/Content/Slate/Fonts/Roboto-Regular.ttf, read at run
    time; nothing is added to this repository.
  - VaCuus.Font.Subpixel.ReplacementAdvance: the engine's replacement box for U+4E00 adds its 7 px
    between two x (LatoLatin has no U+FFFD of its own).
Restore-the-bug, Win64, UE 5.8 host editor, -unattended -nullrhi, 2026-10-16, one hunk at a time:
  - patch absent (Include/ and Source/ at master, the tests kept): LetterSpacing (0 px added),
    FractionalPen (shifts of 0, 1 and 1), LineWidth (its control: "12 words summed to 379 px, drawn
    379 px"), Advance (1200) and Kerning (0 against -46.8) fail; FallbackAdvance and
    ReplacementAdvance pass -- they guard a partial loss, not the whole patch;
  - WeakCopy's line dropped: FallbackAdvance alone fails, 0 px against 13 or 14;
  - the replacement box's line dropped: ReplacementAdvance alone, 0 against 7;
  - FontFaceLayer.h at master: FractionalPen alone, shifts of 0, 1 and 1;
  - ElementText.cpp at master: LineWidth alone, 412 measured against 408 drawn;
  - FT_KERNING_DEFAULT back: Kerning alone, 0 against -46.8;
  - advance_exact from horiAdvance: Advance alone, 1200;
  - (int)letter_spacing back in GetStringWidth and GenerateString: LetterSpacing alone, 0 px added;
  - WidgetTextInput.cpp at master: all seven pass -- no test sees that hunk;
  - patch present: all seven Success, and the rest of VaCuus. green alongside them (286 of 286).

NOT yet offered upstream.

Patch #15 follow-up (owner, landing PR #23) -- defects the review found, each with a test.

1. THE ATLAS GUTTER IS TWO TEXELS. Source/Core/TextureLayoutRow.cpp:19, :32, :53, and the page-size
estimate in TextureLayoutTexture.cpp:33. The sub-pixel quad above samples u from (ink - fraction) to
(ink + width + 1 - fraction) texels. Untransformed, every pixel centre lands half a texel inside
that span and the reads stay within one column of the ink. Under any transform -- a scale, a
rotation, a fractional translate, a transform transition in flight -- a sample can land anywhere
in the span, and bilinear reads floor(s - 0.5) and the column after it: two columns past the ink
on either side, so upstream's one-column gutter let a glyph pick up its neighbour's edge. Upstream's
own rounded quad never needed more than one. Test: VaCuus.Font.Subpixel.AtlasGutter draws every
printable ASCII glyph at pen + 0.25 and + 0.75, reads each quad back as atlas texels and fails if
one quad's reach overlaps another glyph's ink on shared rows. Restore-the-bug, Linux, 2026-10-16:
one-texel gutter -> Fail, "174 glyph pairs ... '!' at pen + 0.25 can read columns 10-15, and 'V'
is drawn from 15-25"; two -> Success. Line shifts: TextureLayoutRow.cpp +4 from old :14;
FontFaceLayer.h +1 from :64 (its comment now names the two-texel gutter).

2. A LINE IS MEASURED ONCE. PR #23 costed a token as W(line + token) - W(line), re-measuring the
line so far for every token: quadratic in the line, and worst where lines are long -- a single-line
input is `white-space: pre` (Elements/WidgetTextInput.cpp:164) and re-formats its whole value on
every keystroke. FontEngineInterface gains GetStringWidthFrom (Include/RmlUi/Core/FontEngineInterface.h
:91-99): GetStringWidth continued from an unrounded pen. The default engine's GetStringWidth is now
that one loop started at 0 (FontFaceHandleDefault.cpp:68-72, :74-102), so a line measured token by
token makes the same float additions in the same order as one call over the line and rounds once;
the base implementation (FontEngineInterface.cpp:54-60) adds GetStringWidth to the pen, i.e. a
custom engine gets upstream's per-token sum. GenerateLine keeps upstream's previous_codepoint for
kerning across a token boundary and carries the pen (ElementText.cpp:254, :259-262, :270-272,
:311-314, :334). Test: VaCuus.Font.Subpixel.LineMeasuredOnce puts U+4E00, which no loaded face has,
first on an eleven-token line; patch #5 counts every lookup of it (FontProvider.cpp:54-57), so the
count is how many times GenerateLine measured that token. Restore-the-bug, Linux, 2026-10-16: PR
#23's `line + token` -> Fail, "looked the first token's character up 11 times"; the continued pen ->
Success, 1 lookup, and VaCuus.Font.Subpixel.LineWidth still finds GenerateLine's width equal to the
line GenerateString draws. Line shifts: ElementText.cpp +11 from old :323 (+1 :253, +4 :257, +2
:262, +3 :304, +1 :323), and patch #9's citations above moved with it; FontFaceHandleDefault.cpp
+6 from old :74; FontEngineInterface.h +10 from :90. Moved in-repo citations, each compared with the
line it named before: ElementText.cpp :425-428, :430-439, :443-446, :530-536, :530-539, :371-374,
:341, :535-536 (+11); FontFaceHandleDefault.cpp :349-352, :378-394, :385-389, :397-404 (+6).

3. AN SBIX FACE KEEPS ITS ADVANCE. Source/Core/FontEngineDefault/FreeTypeInterface.cpp:342-346 takes
advance_exact from linearHoriAdvance only when FT_IS_SCALABLE(ft_face). FreeType converts that field
to 16.16 pixels for a scalable face alone (FreeType 2.14.1 src/base/ftobjs.c:1100-1102). An sbix face
that also has outlines is not scalable (src/sfnt/sfobjs.c:1103-1110) -- Apple's emoji fonts are
built so -- yet its glyph loader still stores the hmtx advance there (src/truetype/ttgload.c:2412),
in font units, and PR #23 read 600 of them as 0.009 px: every glyph of such a face drew on top of
the last. CBDT faces were never affected; their outlines are dropped and the field stays 0. Test:
VaCuus.Font.Subpixel.SbixAdvance loads VaCuus/Private/Tests/VaCuusSbixFixture.h -- 808 bytes from
Tools/gen_sbix_fixture.py, one 'A' with a glyf outline and a 32 ppem sbix bitmap, advance 600/1000
-- and measures "AAAA" at 32 px. Restore-the-bug, Linux, 2026-10-16: the ungated read -> Fail,
"four A from the sbix face measure 1 px, about 77 expected"; gated -> Success. Line shifts:
FreeTypeInterface.cpp +2 from old :344.
